lyrics:
[Intro: solo piano, four simple chords]

[Verse 1: raw, quiet, piano only]
I keep setting out two plates
I keep saving you the news
Every funny thing that happens
Still gets halfway to you

[Pre-Chorus: voice rises, left hand of the piano deepens]
And the phone lights up and it isn't your name
And I put it back down again

[Chorus: full voice, strained, piano louder]
I was somebody's person
Somebody's "call me when you land"
Now there's no one I report to
And I don't know where to put my hands
I was somebody's person
Now I'm just someone

[Verse 2: quiet again, a single cello joins]
There's a coat I haven't moved
There's a mug I haven't cleaned
I've got all the room I wanted
And I don't know what it means

[Pre-Chorus: voice rises, cello swells]
And the door goes click and it's only the wind
And I say your name again

[Chorus: full voice, strings, piano pounding]
I was somebody's person
Somebody's "call me when you land"
Now there's no one I report to
And I don't know where to put my hands
I was somebody's person
Now I'm just someone

[Bridge: almost shouted, voice cracking]
And I'd give anything
To be asked if I got home
To be told to wear a jacket
To be told

[Final Chorus: quietest, piano and voice, then one swell]
I was somebody's person
Somebody's "call me when you land"
Now there's no one I report to
And I don't know where to put my hands
I was somebody's person
I was somebody's

[Outro: piano alone, last chord unresolved]
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 110 BPM, 4/4, D-flat major. Four chords, repeating. Steady and simple, with nowhere to hide.

VOICE: Male tenor, raw and raspy, with a Scottish colour to the vowels. Quiet and conversational in the verses. In the chorus he pushes to the top of his chest voice until it strains and cracks, and he does not hide it. Almost shouted in the bridge, then barely there in the final chorus. No harmonies.

INSTRUMENTS: An acoustic piano playing steady, repeated chords, the only instrument for the first verse. A single cello from verse 2. A small string section in the second chorus. Very soft bass notes. No drums at any point.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, piano. 0:09 Verse 1. 0:31 Pre-chorus. 0:44 Chorus 1. 1:10 Verse 2, with cello. 1:32 Pre-chorus. 1:45 Chorus 2, with strings. 2:11 Bridge, the loudest and rawest singing. 2:28 Final chorus, suddenly quiet, with one swell on the fourth line. 2:58 Outro, piano alone, ending on an unresolved chord at 3:10.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Late-2010s piano ballad: close, warm and plain. The voice is dry enough to hear the breaths and the grain.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The crack in the voice on 'hands' in the first chorus.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The bridge is about being fussed over: told to wear a jacket, asked if you got home. People notice that kind of love once it stops, and it applies to a partner, a parent or a grandparent.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Habit, disorientation, longing, an unfinished sentence.
